title: Integrations
markdown:
External channels connect callers to the Executive. Each inbound adapter resolves the sender to a Person via `find_person_by_{slack,discord,telegram,email}_id` and threads `person_id` into `Executive.chat()`.

### Inbound channels

- **Slack** (`integrations.slack_bot`) — Bolt socket-mode; responds to `@mention`s, DMs, and thread continuations.
- **Discord** (`integrations.discord_bot`) — discord.py gateway embedded in the lifespan; per-thread auto-titling, session-scoped memory, author attribution, configurable `@mention` thread promotion.
- **Telegram** — webhook gating + per-chat history.
- **Google Chat** — webhook + service-account auth.
- **Email** (`integrations.email_poller`) — IMAP poll loop; strips Reply-To, filters auto-replies.

Slack, Discord, and Telegram are roster-gated on inbound: an unrostered sender's message is silently dropped (`details.outcome="rejected_unknown_sender"`). Email is not inbound-gated — non-roster mail flows through with a `[POLICY]` notice so triage can classify it. Slack/Discord thread continuations pass the shared `integrations.response_gate` (utility-fast model, biased toward replying).

### Attachments

`integrations.attachments` handles web chat, Discord, and Telegram. Images become Anthropic vision blocks; documents (PDF/DOCX/TXT/MD/CSV) are inlined and indexed into the ChromaDB `company_docs` collection for future RAG. 20 MB/file cap; web chat uses `POST /chat/upload`.

Indexed chunks are keyed on `attachment:<bare filename>`. An attachment's name is chosen by whoever sent the message, and the name is the chunk-id namespace — unprefixed, an emailed `strategy-2026.md` would upsert straight over the curated company document of that name. The prefix keeps inbound content in its own namespace and makes its provenance visible in the `[filename]` retrieval citation.

They carry the domain `company_docs`, which is deliberately **not** one of the specialist domains: the chunks match no domain filter, so they do not currently reach the Executive. Anyone who can attach a file in an integration channel would otherwise be writing into every specialist's context, and these rows have no removal path — they are never written to `company/docs/`, so `GET /documents` does not list them and `DELETE /documents/{filename}` 404s before reaching the store. Making them retrievable is a trust-boundary change that needs a delete path alongside it.

### MCP gateway & outbound

MCP runs in **both directions**. As a *client*, `orchestrator.mcp_gateway.MCPGateway` proxies MCP servers (Gmail, Calendar, Drive — whatever `mcp_servers.json` configures) as Executive tools, with egress gating on Gmail recipients, Calendar attendees, and Drive share grantees against the roster (and a refusal of public / whole-domain Drive sharing). The Google Workspace server (`workspace-mcp`) behind those Gmail/Calendar/Drive tools runs **co-located inside the API** as a stdio child of the gateway — fitting the single-tenant model (one install = one company = one exec Google account), so there's no separate service to operate. It's baked into the API image and launched by `docker/workspace-mcp-launch.sh`, which selects single-user OAuth (token persisted at `/data/google_credentials`) or service-account domain-wide delegation from `GWORKSPACE_AUTH_MODE`. The gateway forwards the Google secrets to the child via `_FORWARDED_ENV_VARS`. As a *server*, `openexecutive.mcp_server` exposes OE's own company context and specialist council to external MCP clients at `/mcp` — the inverse direction; see the dedicated **MCP Server** section. The gateway launches extensible-mcp as a `uvx` subprocess whose fastembed tool-search index uses an embedding model baked into the API image and loaded offline, so it no longer re-downloads that model from the Hugging Face Hub on every cold start. Because the MCP stdio client does not inherit the parent environment, `MCPGateway.start()` explicitly forwards the embedding-cache/offline env vars (`FASTEMBED_CACHE_PATH`, `HF_HUB_OFFLINE`, …) into the child. Outbound tools: per-Person DMs (`send_slack_dm`, `send_discord_dm`, `send_telegram_message`) plus room-targeted `send_department_message` and `send_company_broadcast`. The per-Person DMs are additionally rate-limited and de-duplicated by the outbound anti-spam guard (below).

### Outbound anti-spam guard

Every per-Person DM passes a deterministic guard (`orchestrator.outbound_guard.check_outbound_allowed`) after the roster gate and recipient-id recovery but before the network send — the single chokepoint **all** proactive DM paths reach (ad-hoc chat sends, the scheduler's followup/nudge dispatch, principal-brief delivery, the reflection turn, and research-finding routing). On a violation it returns a human-readable reason and the handler **suppresses** the send (`{"status":"suppressed","reason":…}`), writes a `tool_invocation` audit row with `suppressed=true`, and writes **no** `done` activity row — so a blocked attempt never counts toward its own rate cap, and the Executive can read the reason and hold or `schedule_followup` for the recipient's next window. Three controls: **content dedup** (a near-identical message — whitespace/case-normalized, first 160 chars — already sent to the same recipient within `OUTBOUND_DEDUP_WINDOW_MINUTES`, default 360); a **per-recipient rate cap** (`OUTBOUND_MAX_PER_RECIPIENT_PER_WINDOW`, default 5, over `OUTBOUND_RATE_WINDOW_MINUTES`, default 60); and **quiet hours / availability** (`OUTBOUND_RESPECT_QUIET_HOURS`, default on — refuse while the recipient is on leave or outside their `people.channel` availability windows, surfacing the next open window). Delivery history is read from the existing `status='done'` `scheduled_actions` rows (`episodic.recent_sends_for_channel_ref`), so there is no new table. The guard is **fail-open**: any internal lookup error returns "allow", so it can never turn a working send into a crash or a silently-dropped message. Principal briefs and the internal heartbeat kinds use the `__internal__` channel and never reach these handlers, so they are unaffected.

### Calendar & Google Meet

The Executive books meetings through two typed tools over the Calendar MCP. `create_calendar_event` schedules a **future** meeting (propose→approve by default, or auto-execute once that decision class is promoted) and may be used proactively when a stalled goal warrants a sync. `create_instant_meeting` spins up an **impromptu call starting now**, auto-executing without the approval step and skipping the business-hours/horizon caps, so the Executive can hand back a join link immediately. Both attach a **Google Meet** link by default (`add_google_meet`; opt out for in-person), parsed from the created event's `conferenceData` and surfaced to the caller plus persisted on the decision ledger. Either way the caps that matter still hold — roster membership, principal-protection, max attendees, and a daily booking ceiling.

**Around-the-meeting participation.** The Executive doesn't join the call as a live voice; instead, on every successful booking it schedules a best-effort post-meeting follow-up (~5 min after the end) that DMs a human attendee asking for a quick recap — key decisions and action items. The reply flows back through the same cross-session DM context linkage described below, so the Executive can act on it (summarize, follow up) in a later turn. No meeting-transcript or Drive integration is required.

### Cross-session DM context

When the principal says "DM Alex about X" in one session, OE sends the DM and — if a live conversation is active — records an `outbound_context` linkage row (recipient, full outbound text, originating session id). Email is covered too but recorded one layer deeper — there is no `send_email` tool, so the linkage is written in `orchestrator.mcp_gateway` after a successful `google_workspace__send_gmail_message`, one row per `to`/`cc` recipient keyed by the bare lowercased address (OE's own address skipped). When Alex later replies on the 1:1 DM path — or by email — the shared helper `integrations.inbound_hydration.hydrate_user_message` (called by the Discord, Telegram, and Slack handlers, and by the email poller keyed on the sender address) looks up the most-recent `open` linkage for that sender within 72h and prepends an `<outbound_reply_context>` block — the outbound text plus a backstory excerpt from the originating session — to the message handed to `Executive.chat()`. So OE knows what the reply is about instead of starting from an empty per-person session. The block lands in the user turn (caching rule) and is injected into a copy only — the pristine reply is persisted to history. The linkage is one-shot (consumed on first matched reply, race-safe) so an unrelated later DM isn't re-hydrated. This is deterministic and independent of the per-person `peer_memory` (Honcho) layer.
